$schema_note: Ground truth for the SAU-302 §8 calibration check. Each entry is a deliberately hard column: the source Postgres type, the EXPECTED-correct Snowflake target representation, the trap a naive mapper falls into, and the verification assertion the core loop (child #2) must satisfy. 'confidence_floor' is the minimum calibrated confidence the mapper should report when it gets this right.

hard_columns.trap: fixed-width PII with leading zeros ('0042','0007') — must NOT be coerced to NUMBER, which drops leading zeros and changes identity
hard_columns.assert: byte-identical string preserved incl. leading zeros

hard_columns.trap: leading-zero last4 ('0019','0007') — numeric coercion is lossy
hard_columns.assert: string preserved

hard_columns.trap: fixed-width hex with leading zeros; must stay textual identity
hard_columns.assert: string preserved

hard_columns.trap: timestamp WITHOUT time zone — mapping to TIMESTAMP_TZ invents an offset and shifts values
hard_columns.assert: wall-clock value preserved, no tz applied

hard_columns.trap: tz-aware; offsets (+00,+02,+09) must round-trip to the same instant
hard_columns.assert: same UTC instant preserved

hard_columns.trap: high-precision currency; FLOAT mapping loses exactness at the 99999999.9999 boundary and sub-cent 0.0001
hard_columns.assert: exact decimal, scale 4 preserved at boundaries

hard_columns.trap: 6-dp rate (0.083325) — float rounding corrupts the 6th place
hard_columns.assert: scale 6 preserved

hard_columns.trap: money stored as integer cents (24990000) — must remain integer, never FLOAT
hard_columns.assert: exact integer preserved

hard_columns.trap: currency; JPY plan stored 2dp though currency is zero-dp — mapper must preserve source scale, not infer from currency
hard_columns.assert: scale 2 preserved

hard_columns.trap: REAL (float4) 2.4500001 — FLOAT is acceptable but mapper must FLAG lossy float identity (not assert byte-equality)
hard_columns.assert: approximate-equality within float4 epsilon; flagged lossy

hard_columns.trap: fraction scale-4 (0.1000) — must keep trailing-zero scale
hard_columns.assert: scale 4 preserved

hard_columns.trap: nested JSON (geo object) — flattening to VARCHAR loses structure/queryability
hard_columns.assert: round-trips as parseable VARIANT, nested keys intact

hard_columns.trap: JSON with unicode + emoji ('🚀') — encoding must survive
hard_columns.assert: unicode/emoji preserved in VARIANT

hard_columns.trap: text array — must map to ARRAY, not a delimited VARCHAR
hard_columns.assert: element count + values preserved as ARRAY

hard_columns.trap: array of NUMERICs — elements must keep scale 2 inside the ARRAY
hard_columns.assert: numeric elements preserve scale in ARRAY

hard_columns.trap: INET (incl. IPv6 '2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334' and '::1') has no Snowflake native type — must serialize losslessly to text
hard_columns.assert: canonical text form preserved (IPv4 + IPv6)

hard_columns.trap: numeric-LOOKING text ('1234.5600','89,95') — must NOT be auto-parsed to a number; comma-decimal would corrupt
hard_columns.assert: kept as text verbatim; mapper must NOT infer numeric

hard_columns.trap: PII; length boundary (RFC max 320) — must preserve full length, governance-tag as PII
hard_columns.assert: full value preserved, length cap honored

hard_columns.trap: geo double — FLOAT acceptable; flag float identity not byte-equality
hard_columns.assert: approximate-equality within float8 epsilon

hard_columns.trap: Postgres enum — Snowflake has no native enum; must preserve the label set and reject unknowns
hard_columns.assert: enum label preserved; domain enforced via CHECK/ref
